Whistleblowers claim that the U.S. government is operating a classified UFO crash retrieval and reverse engineering program. The Pentagon’s official UFO office (@DoD_AARO) says it investigated and found no evidence of any secret UFO programs. Are they telling the truth? Here’s a chronological timeline of 100 examples where U.S. defense and intelligence agencies lied to Congress and the public.

2021: The Pentagon said a drone strike in Kabul killed ISIS terrorists, it actually killed ten civilians including seven children.

2019: Officials concealed the fact that U.S. bombs killed dozens of civilians in Baghuz Syria.

2018: The Pentagon denied deep involvement in the Saudi-led war in Yemen, records later proved it refueled and coordinated airstrikes.

2017: They claimed precision in Mosul operations, but U.S. bombs destroyed entire neighborhoods and killed hundreds.

2016: Leaders said there were “no boots on the ground” in Syria, U.S. troops were already fighting there.

2015: The Pentagon said a hospital in Kunduz Afghanistan was hit by mistake, evidence showed repeated targeting calls during the attack.

2014: They reported low civilian casualties in the ISIS war, later data proved thousands had died.

2013: Defense officials said surveillance targeted foreigners, the NSA was spying on Americans too.

2012: The Pentagon denied drone strikes killed civilians in Pakistan and Yemen, its own memos confirmed civilian deaths.

2011: Officials said the Libya mission was to protect civilians, it was a covert regime-change war.

2010: They claimed transparency in Iraq, but withheld reports documenting tens of thousands of civilian deaths.

2009: Generals told the public the Afghanistan surge was succeeding, internal reviews admitted the opposite.

2007: The Pentagon said civilian casualties in Iraq were decreasing, leaked numbers showed increases.

2006: They called the Haditha killings a firefight, investigations proved U.S. Marines executed civilians.

2005: Officials denied any torture by U.S. forces, classified files proved widespread abuse.

2004: The Pentagon blamed “a few bad apples” for Abu Ghraib, torture was ordered through command channels.

2004: They denied using banned munitions in Fallujah, evidence showed white phosphorus was used on civilians.

2004: The Jessica Lynch “rescue” was staged, officials fabricated her hero story for propaganda.

2004: They told Pat Tillman’s family he died heroically in combat, it was friendly fire deliberately covered up.

2003: The Pentagon insisted Iraq had active weapons of mass destruction, none existed.

2003: Officials said “shock and awe” bombing was surgical, it leveled cities and killed thousands.

2002: They denied running secret prisons, black-site torture was later confirmed.

2002: Officials said detainees in Bagram were treated humanely, two were beaten to death.

2001: The Pentagon told Congress Afghanistan would be a short limited war, it lasted twenty years.

2001: They said the U.S. was not spying on its citizens, warrantless surveillance began immediately after 9/11.

1999: Officials claimed NATO bombs in Kosovo were precise, hundreds of civilians were killed.

1996: They denied chemical exposure during weapons tests on U.S. troops, later declassified reports proved exposure.

1995: The Pentagon dismissed Gulf War Illness as psychological, toxic exposures were later documented.

1994: Officials said the Haiti mission was peacekeeping, it was a military occupation.

1993: They described Somalia as humanitarian aid, it was a combat mission that ended in Black Hawk Down.

1991: The Pentagon denied U.S. troops were exposed to sarin gas at Khamisiyah, sensors showed contamination.

1991: They called Gulf War bombing “surgical,” civilian infrastructure was systematically destroyed.

1990: Officials said Panama’s invasion was to arrest one man, thousands of civilians were killed.

1989: The Pentagon denied abuses at Philippine bases, later testimony revealed systemic crimes.

1987: They claimed ignorance of Iran-Contra arms trafficking, Pentagon records showed involvement.

1986: Officials said the Libya airstrikes hit only military targets, civilians were bombed.

1985: They denied aiding Nicaraguan Contras, funding and logistics were traced back to DoD.

1984: The Pentagon defended the School of the Americas, its graduates led death squads.

1983: They said the Grenada invasion rescued students, it was planned before the crisis.

1982: Officials denied supporting Salvadoran death squads, training and weapons came from the U.S.

1981: They denied covert operations in Nicaragua, CIA and Pentagon documents proved otherwise.

1979: NATO leaders minimized nuclear-deployment risks, Pentagon analyses warned of catastrophe.

1976: They denied DoD links to illegal human testing, Army and CIA experiments were later exposed.

1975: Officials said the Cambodia evacuation was orderly, chaos and abandonment were covered up.

1973: The Pentagon said bombing halted to advance peace, raids continued in secret.

1972: They claimed B-52 bombing was effective and limited, civilian areas were destroyed by thousands of tons of bombs.

1971: The Pentagon Papers proved decades of lies about Vietnam.

1971: Officials insisted Agent Orange was safe, it caused cancers and birth defects.

1970: They said the U.S. respected Cambodia’s borders, American forces invaded that year.

1969: The Pentagon denied a massacre at My Lai, soldiers had executed over 500 unarmed civilians.

1969: Officials said Vietnamization was succeeding, U.S. intelligence knew South Vietnam could not survive withdrawal.

1968: They released fake body counts to show victory, the numbers were fabricated.

1968: They called the Tet Offensive an enemy defeat, it was a strategic disaster for U.S. forces.

1967: The Pentagon denied civilian assassinations under the Phoenix Program, thousands were killed.

1966: They said the U.S. was not bombing Laos, hundreds of thousands of bombs were dropped.

1965: Officials claimed the Dominican Republic intervention was to protect Americans, it was to crush a democratic uprising.

1964: They said North Vietnam attacked twice in the Gulf of Tonkin, the second attack never happened.

1963: The Pentagon called U.S. forces in Vietnam “advisors,” they were leading combat missions.

1962: Officials drafted plans for fake terrorist attacks called Operation Northwoods, to justify war with Cuba.

1962: They told sailors Project SHAD tests were safe, the experiments used chemical and biological agents.

1961: The Pentagon denied involvement in the Bay of Pigs invasion, it had helped plan and support it.

1960: They said a U-2 plane was a weather aircraft, it was a spy plane shot down over the USSR.

1959: They told troops nuclear tests were harmless, soldiers were exposed to lethal radiation.

1958: They said the Lebanon deployment was peacekeeping, it was to secure a pro-U.S. regime.

1957: Officials warned of a “missile gap” with the Soviets, internal data showed the U.S. was far ahead.

1956: The Pentagon said atomic tests in the Pacific were safe, islanders were poisoned by fallout.

1955: They denied human experimentation, Edgewood Arsenal tested nerve gas on soldiers.

1954: They said the U.S. had no role in Guatemala’s coup, it was organized and backed by U.S. forces.

1953: They denied abuse of North Korean POWs, evidence later showed widespread violations.

1952: Officials said atomic field tests were controlled, soldiers were ordered to march through nuclear blasts.

1951: They called the Korean War a “limited conflict,” casualties exceeded two million.

1950: They said the North Korean invasion was a surprise, intelligence had warned weeks before.

1949: They claimed NATO was defensive, secret plans already included nuclear first strikes.

1948: Officials said the Berlin airlift carried only food, it also moved military supplies.

1947: The Pentagon dismissed early UFO reports as weather balloons, internal files showed ongoing investigations.

1947: They said Operation Paperclip brought harmless scientists, many were high-ranking Nazis.

1946: Officials told sailors Bikini tests were safe, radiation killed and sickened participants.

1945: They said atomic bomb tests posed no danger to troops, radiation victims were denied care.

1945: They said only military targets were bombed in Japan, entire civilian cities were destroyed.

1944: They said friendly-fire losses were minimal in Normandy, thousands were killed by U.S. fire.

1943: Officials said Black pilots lacked skill, the Tuskegee Airmen proved them wrong in combat.

1943: They told troops mustard gas drills were harmless, soldiers suffered burns and poisoning.

1942: They claimed Japanese internment was for security, it was driven by racism and hysteria.

1942: They said Manila and Corregidor fell after fierce defense, leaders had abandoned the troops.

1941: They claimed Pearl Harbor was a complete surprise, intelligence warnings were ignored.

1941: They said the Atlantic Charter kept the U.S. neutral, Roosevelt had already committed to war.

1940: They told the public Lend-Lease was not military aid, it was preparation for U.S. entry into WWII.

1939: Officials downplayed rearmament costs, military budgets exploded in secret.

1937: They claimed compliance with chemical weapons bans, new stockpiles were being built.

1935: They said war games were for defense, they were designed to justify larger budgets.

1932: They blamed veterans for the Bonus Army violence, U.S. troops burned their camps.

1918: They said troop movements did not spread influenza, the Army helped cause the pandemic.

1917: They claimed WWI would be short and glorious, it became one of the deadliest wars in history.

1899: They said the Philippine-American War was liberation, it was brutal colonial conquest.

1864: They said prisoners were treated humanely, thousands died of neglect and starvation.

1846: They claimed Mexico started the war, U.S. troops had invaded Mexican territory first.

1812: They promised readiness for war with Britain, troops lacked weapons and supplies.

1778: They said shortages were minor, soldiers starved through the winter at Valley Forge.

1776: They claimed the Continental Army was strong and supplied, it was disorganized and underfed.

1775: They told the colonies the war would be short and easy, it lasted eight years.
